title: Those who know
scope: Relative-correlative clauses of time (जब … तब/तो, जब भी, तभी, जब से … तब से, जब तक … तब तक, जब तक … नहीं … तब तक, जैसे ही … वैसे ही, ज्योंही … त्योंही); infinitive + चाहिए “should” with को and agreement with the object (no agreement after a को object, था); infinitive + होना “am to” and + पड़ना “must” (पड़ा, पड़ता है, पड़ेगा); relative जो … वह with oblique जिस, जिसने, जिन, जिन्होंने, जिसे, जिन्हें, each pronoun in the case of its own clause; जो कोई, जो कुछ, जो भी, archaic सो; मिलना “to get, be available”, chance meetings (मुझे सीता मिली), मिलना-जुलना, मिल-जुलकर; लगना “to strike, seem, be felt, be taken (of time)”

vocab.en: for as long as … for that long
since the time when … since then
at that very time, just then
the moment that … at that moment
to strike, seem; to be attached; to be taken (of time)

lessons.title: जब … तब
lessons.desc: Relative clauses of time: “when … then”, “until”, “as soon as”

items.q: Fill the gap: “When Raj comes, then we will eat.”
items.hi: ___ राज आएगा तब हम खाना खाएँगे ।
items.say: जब राज आएगा तब हम खाना खाएँगे ।
items.en: When[0] Raj[1] comes[2], {then}[3] we[4] {will eat}[5+6].
wrong: कब
कब is the question word “when?”. The relative “when” begins with j-, जब.
तब
तब is the correlative “then”, which opens the second clause.
items.why: Relative and correlative: the जब clause (“when”, starting with j-) usually comes first, and the correlative तब (“then”) picks it up. तब is often replaced by तो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “When Father came from the office, then we had tea.”
items.hi: जब पिता जी दफ़्तर से आए ___ हमने चाय पी ।
items.say: जब पिता जी दफ़्तर से आए तब हमने चाय पी ।
items.en: When[0] Father[1+2] came[5] {from the office}[3+4], {then}[6] we[7] had[9] tea[8].
wrong: कब
कब is the question word. The correlative “then” is तब.
जब
जब opens the first clause. The second clause takes the correlative तब.
items.why: Relative and correlative: the जब clause (“when”, starting with j-) usually comes first, and the correlative तब (“then”) picks it up. तब is often replaced by तो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Ever since Sita went to Delhi, from then on she has been very happy.”
items.hi: जब से सीता दिल्ली गई है ___ वह बहुत ख़ुश है ।
items.say: जब से सीता दिल्ली गई है तब से वह बहुत ख़ुश है ।
items.en: {Ever since}[0+1] Sita[2] went[4+5] to Delhi[3], {from then on}[6+7] she[8] {has been}[11] very[9] happy[10].
wrong: तब तक
तब तक “for that long” pairs with जब तक. जब से pairs with तब से.
कब से
कब से is the question “since when?”. The correlative begins with t-, तब से.
items.why: The pairs are जब … तब “when … then”, जब से … तब से “since … since then”, जब तक … तब तक “as long as … for that long”, जब तक … नहीं … तब तक “until”, जैसे ही … वैसे ही “as soon as”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “As long as you are here, for that long I have no fear.”
items.hi: जब तक तुम यहाँ हो ___ मुझे कोई डर नहीं है ।
items.say: जब तक तुम यहाँ हो तब तक मुझे कोई डर नहीं है ।
items.en: {As long as}[0+1] you[2] are[4] here[3], {for that long}[5+6] I[7] {have no}[8+10+11] fear[9].
wrong: तब से
तब से “since then” pairs with जब से. जब तक pairs with तब तक.
कब तक
कब तक is the question “until when?”. The correlative begins with t-, तब तक.
items.why: The pairs are जब … तब “when … then”, जब से … तब से “since … since then”, जब तक … तब तक “as long as … for that long”, जब तक … नहीं … तब तक “until”, जैसे ही … वैसे ही “as soon as”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जब तक डाक्टर नहीं आएगा तब तक सीता बच्चे के पास रहेगी ।
items.a: Sita will stay with the child until the doctor comes.
wrong: Sita will stay with the child while the doctor is there.
जब तक … नहीं means “until”: the doctor has not come yet.
Sita will go to the child when the doctor comes.
That would be जब … तब. जब तक … नहीं … तब तक is “until … until then”.
items.why: जब तक … नहीं … तब तक “until … until then”, literally “as long as … not …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “As soon as I reached home, just then it began to rain. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: जैसे ही मैं घर पहुँचा ___ बारिश शुरू हो गई ।
items.say: जैसे ही मैं घर पहुँचा वैसे ही बारिश शुरू हो गई ।
items.en: {As soon as}[0+1] I[2] reached[4] home[3], {just then}[5+6] {it began}[8+9+10] to rain[7]. (a man speaking)
wrong: तब से
तब से “since then” pairs with जब से. जैसे ही pairs with वैसे ही.
जैसे ही
जैसे ही opens the first clause. The second takes the correlative वैसे ही.
items.why: जैसे ही … वैसे ही, or ज्योंही … त्योंही, “as soon as … then”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Whenever Mohan comes, he brings something.”
items.hi: जब ___ मोहन आता है, वह कुछ न कुछ लाता है ।
items.say: जब भी मोहन आता है, वह कुछ न कुछ लाता है ।
items.en: Whenever[0+1] Mohan[2] comes[3+4], he[5] brings[9+10] something[6+7+8].
wrong: तक
जब तक is “as long as”. “Whenever” is जब भी.
से
जब से is “since”. “Whenever” is जब भी.
items.why: जब भी “whenever” is the emphatic form of जब.

items.q: What does तभी mean?
items.a: at that very time, just then
wrong: whenever
“Whenever” is जब भी.
since then
“Since then” is तब से.
items.why: तभी is तब + ही, “at that very time”, as अभी is अब + ही.

items.q: Join the two sentences with जब … तब
items.a: जब माँ फ़ोन करेंगी तब मैं उन्हें सब कुछ बताऊँगा ।
wrong: कब माँ फ़ोन करेंगी तब मैं उन्हें सब कुछ बताऊँगा ।
कब is the question word “when?”. The relative is जब.
जब माँ फ़ोन करेंगी जब मैं उन्हें सब कुछ बताऊँगा ।
The second clause takes the correlative तब, not जब.
items.why: Relative and correlative: the जब clause (“when”, starting with j-) usually comes first, and the correlative तब (“then”) picks it up. तब is often replaced by तो.
items.hi: माँ फ़ोन करेंगी । मैं उन्हें सब कुछ बताऊँगा ।
items.say: जब माँ फ़ोन करेंगी तब मैं उन्हें सब कुछ बताऊँगा ।
items.en: When[0] Mother[1] phones[2+3], {then}[4] I[5] {will tell}[9] her[6] everything[7+8]. (a man speaking)

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जब मैं छोटा था तब हम गाँव में रहते थे ।
items.a: When I was little, we lived in a village.
wrong: Since I was little, we have lived in a village.
That would be जब से … तब से.
As long as I am little, we will live in a village.
That would be जब तक … तब तक, with future verbs.
items.why: Relative and correlative: the जब clause (“when”, starting with j-) usually comes first, and the correlative तब (“then”) picks it up. तब is often replaced by तो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan should take his medicine every day.”
items.hi: ___ रोज़ दवा लेनी चाहिए ।
items.say: मोहन को रोज़ दवा लेनी चाहिए ।
items.en: Mohan[0+1] should[5] take[4] {his medicine}[3] {every day}[2].
wrong: मोहन
The person who should do something takes को — मोहन को.
मोहन ने
ने marks the doer of a transitive verb in the perfective. With चाहिए the person takes को.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj should wash his clothes himself.”
items.hi: राज को अपने कपड़े ख़ुद ___ चाहिए ।
items.say: राज को अपने कपड़े ख़ुद धोने चाहिए ।
items.en: Raj[0+1] should[6] wash[5] his[2] clothes[3] himself[4].
wrong: धोनी
धोनी is feminine. The infinitive agrees with कपड़े, masculine plural, so धोने.
धोते
धोते is the imperfective participle. चाहिए “should” follows the infinitive.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita should listen to her mother (lit. “hear her mother's word”).”
items.hi: सीता को अपनी माँ की बात ___ चाहिए ।
items.say: सीता को अपनी माँ की बात सुननी चाहिए ।
items.en: Sita[0+1] should[7] listen[6] to her[2] mother[3+4] (lit. “hear her mother's word[5]”).
wrong: सुनने
सुनने is the masculine plural or oblique form. The infinitive agrees with बात, feminine singular: सुननी.
सुनती
सुनती is the imperfective participle. चाहिए “should” follows the infinitive.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We should have seen that film yesterday.”
items.hi: हमें कल वह फ़िल्म देखनी चाहिए ___ ।
items.say: हमें कल वह फ़िल्म देखनी चाहिए थी ।
items.en: We[0] {should have}[5+6] seen[4] that[2] film[3] yesterday[1].
wrong: था
था is masculine. The auxiliary agrees with फ़िल्म, feminine, as the infinitive देखनी does.
थे
थे is masculine plural. फ़िल्म is feminine singular.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We should have brought the guests from the station.”
items.hi: हमें मेहमानों को स्टेशन से ___ चाहिए था ।
items.say: हमें मेहमानों को स्टेशन से लाना चाहिए था ।
items.en: We[0] {should have}[6+7] brought[5] the guests[1+2] {from the station}[3+4].
wrong: लाने
The object मेहमानों has को, so the infinitive does not agree with it: लाना.
लाया
लाया is the perfective participle. चाहिए follows the infinitive.
items.why: If the direct object takes को, the infinitive does not agree: it stays in -nā, and the past auxiliary is always था.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You should have invited your sister.”
items.hi: आप को अपनी बहिन को बुलाना चाहिए ___ ।
items.say: आप को अपनी बहिन को बुलाना चाहिए था ।
items.en: You[0+1] {should have}[6+7] invited[5] your[2] sister[3+4].
wrong: थी
With को on the object (बहिन को) the auxiliary does not agree with it: it is always था.
थीं is feminine plural. With को on the object the auxiliary is always था.
items.why: If the direct object takes को, the infinitive does not agree: it stays in -nā, and the past auxiliary is always था.

items.q: Fill the gap: “All the windows should stay shut at night.”
items.hi: रात को सारी खिड़कियाँ बंद ___ चाहिए ।
items.say: रात को सारी खिड़कियाँ बंद रहनी चाहिए ।
items.en: All[2] the windows[3] should[6] stay[5] shut[4] {at night}[0+1].
wrong: रहने
रहने is masculine. रहना agrees with its subject खिड़कियाँ, feminine: रहनी.
रहती
रहती is the imperfective participle. चाहिए “should” follows the infinitive.
items.why: With intransitive verbs such as होना and रहना the infinitive can agree with a subject, without को — things are under no moral compulsion.

items.q: Which sentence means “Sita should buy a new sari”?
items.a: सीता को नई साड़ी ख़रीदनी चाहिए ।
wrong: सीता को नई साड़ी चाहिए ।
With a noun alone चाहिए means “is needed”: “Sita needs a new sari”.
सीता नई साड़ी ख़रीदना चाहती है ।
चाहना is “to want”: “Sita wants to buy a new sari”.
सीता को नई साड़ी ख़रीदनी चाहिती है ।
Not a word. चाहिए never changes for gender or person, and it takes no है. चाहती, from चाहना, means “wants”.
items.why: चाहिए with a noun is “is needed”, with an infinitive “should”. चाहना is “to want”.
items.say: सीता को नई साड़ी ख़रीदनी चाहिए ।
items.en: Sita[0+1] should[5] buy[4] a new[2] sari[3].

items.q: Make this a चाहिए sentence
items.a: आप को डाक्टर से मिलना चाहिए ।
wrong: आप डाक्टर से मिलना चाहिए ।
The person who should do something takes को — आप को.
आप को डाक्टर से मिलनी चाहिए ।
मिलना here has no direct object (डाक्टर takes से), so the infinitive stays -nā.
आप को डाक्टर से मिलना चाहिया ।
Not a word. चाहिए is fixed in form and does not change to -yā.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.
items.hi: आप डाक्टर से मिलें ।
items.say: आप को डाक्टर से मिलना चाहिए ।
items.en: You[0+1] should[5] see[3+4] the doctor[2].

items.q: Fill the gap: “They should have thought about these things earlier.”
items.hi: उन्हें ये बातें पहले सोचनी चाहिए ___ ।
items.say: उन्हें ये बातें पहले सोचनी चाहिए थीं ।
items.en: They[0] {should have}[5+6] thought[4] about these[1] things[2] earlier[3].
wrong: थी
थी is singular. The auxiliary agrees with बातें, feminine plural.
था
था is used only when there is no direct object or the object takes को. बातें is a feminine plural object.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

lessons.title: जाना है, जाना पड़ेगा
lessons.desc: Infinitive + होना and पड़ना “have to, must”

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have to see the doctor this evening.”
items.hi: मुझे आज शाम को डाक्टर से ___ है ।
items.say: मुझे आज शाम को डाक्टर से मिलना है ।
items.en: I[0] {have to}[7] see[5+6] the doctor[4] {this evening}[1+2+3].
wrong: मिलता
मिलता is the imperfective participle. “Have to” is the infinitive + है, मिलना है.
मिलने
मिलने is the oblique or plural form. मिलना has no direct object here (डाक्टर takes से), so it stays मिलना.
items.why: Infinitive + होना (है, था, होगा) “am to, have to” is a mild, matter-of-course compulsion. Infinitive + पड़ना is an outside compulsion. The person takes को, and agreement works as with चाहिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My key got lost, so I had to go in through the window.”
items.hi: मेरी चाबी खो गई, इस लिए मुझे खिड़की से अंदर जाना ___ ।
items.say: मेरी चाबी खो गई, इस लिए मुझे खिड़की से अंदर जाना पड़ा ।
items.en: My[0] key[1] {got lost}[2+3], so[4+5] I[6] {had to}[11] go[10] in[9] through[8] the window[7].
wrong: पड़ी
पड़ी is feminine. जाना has no object, so पड़ना is masculine singular: पड़ा.
पड़ता
पड़ता is the imperfective, for a regular compulsion. This happened once, unplanned: पड़ा.
पड़या
Not a word. पड़ना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is पड़ा, with no -y-.
items.why: पड़ा is an unplanned or unwelcome compulsion in the past, पड़ता है a regular one, पड़ेगा a strong one in the future.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj had to buy a new sari.”
items.hi: राज को नई साड़ी ख़रीदनी ___ ।
items.say: राज को नई साड़ी ख़रीदनी पड़ी ।
items.en: Raj[0+1] {had to}[5] buy[4] a new[2] sari[3].
wrong: पड़ा
पड़ा is masculine. पड़ना agrees with साड़ी, feminine, as ख़रीदनी does.
पड़े
पड़े is masculine plural. साड़ी is feminine singular.
items.why: Infinitive + होना (है, था, होगा) “am to, have to” is a mild, matter-of-course compulsion. Infinitive + पड़ना is an outside compulsion. The person takes को, and agreement works as with चाहिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita has to get up at five every morning.”
items.hi: सीता को रोज़ सुबह पाँच बजे उठना ___ है ।
items.say: सीता को रोज़ सुबह पाँच बजे उठना पड़ता है ।
items.en: Sita[0+1] {has to}[7+8] {get up}[6] at[5] five[4] every[2] morning[3].
wrong: पड़ती
पड़ती is feminine. उठना has no object, so पड़ना is masculine singular, whoever the person is.
पड़ते
पड़ते is plural. With no object पड़ना is masculine singular.
items.why: पड़ा is an unplanned or unwelcome compulsion in the past, पड़ता है a regular one, पड़ेगा a strong one in the future.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you want to pass the exam, then you will have to study every day.”
items.hi: अगर तुम परीक्षा पास करना चाहते हो तो तुम्हें रोज़ पढ़ना ___ ।
items.say: अगर तुम परीक्षा पास करना चाहते हो तो तुम्हें रोज़ पढ़ना पड़ेगा ।
items.en: If[0] you[1] want[5+6] to pass[3+4] the exam[2], {then}[7] you[8] {will have to}[11] study[10] {every day}[9].
wrong: पड़ेगी
पड़ेगी is feminine. पढ़ना has no object here, so पड़ना is masculine singular.
पड़ेंगे
पड़ेंगे is plural. With no object पड़ना is masculine singular.
पड़नेगा
Not a word. The future is built on the stem, not the oblique infinitive, giving पड़ेगा.
items.why: पड़ा is an unplanned or unwelcome compulsion in the past, पड़ता है a regular one, पड़ेगा a strong one in the future.

items.q: Which sentence suggests the strongest outside compulsion?
wrong: उसे लौटना चाहिए ।
चाहिए is a moral “should”: “He should go back”.
उसे लौटना है ।
होना is a neutral, matter-of-course “is to”: “He is to go back”.
items.why: चाहिए “should” (moral), है “is to” (neutral), पड़ेगा “will have to” (strong, from outside).
items.say: उसे लौटना पड़ेगा ।
items.en: He[0] {will have to}[2] {go back}[1].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: क्या तुम्हें कुछ ख़रीदना है ?
items.a: Is there something you need to buy?
wrong: Did you buy something?
That would be the perfective: क्या तुमने कुछ ख़रीदा ?
Can you buy something?
That would be सकना — क्या तुम कुछ ख़रीद सकते हो ?
items.why: Infinitive + है can express simple intention or a planned task: “Are you to buy something?”

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan has to go back to Lucknow tomorrow.”
items.hi: ___ कल लखनऊ लौटना है ।
items.say: मोहन को कल लखनऊ लौटना है ।
items.en: Mohan[0+1] {has to}[5] {go back}[4] to Lucknow[3] tomorrow[2].
wrong: मोहन ने
In standard Hindi the person takes को. ने here is regional (Delhi) usage, not standard.
मोहन
The person who has to do something takes को, so मोहन को.
items.why: Infinitive + होना (है, था, होगा) “am to, have to” is a mild, matter-of-course compulsion. Infinitive + पड़ना is an outside compulsion. The person takes को, and agreement works as with चाहिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “She had to write all the letters again.”
items.hi: उसे सारी चिट्ठियाँ फिर से लिखनी ___ ।
items.say: उसे सारी चिट्ठियाँ फिर से लिखनी पड़ीं ।
items.en: She[0] {had to}[6] write[5] all[1] the letters[2] again[3+4].
wrong: पड़ी
पड़ी is singular. पड़ना agrees with चिट्ठियाँ, feminine plural, and the nasal goes on the last word.
पड़े
पड़े is masculine plural. चिट्ठियाँ is feminine.
items.why: Infinitive + होना (है, था, होगा) “am to, have to” is a mild, matter-of-course compulsion. Infinitive + पड़ना is an outside compulsion. The person takes को, and agreement works as with चाहिए.

items.q: Raj missed the bus. Which sentence says he had to walk to the office?
items.a: राज को चलकर दफ़्तर जाना पड़ा ।
wrong: राज को चलकर दफ़्तर जाना चाहिए था ।
चाहिए था is “should have”: it says he ought to have walked, not that he did.
राज चलकर दफ़्तर जाना पड़ा ।
The person who has to do something takes को — राज को.
items.why: पड़ा is an unplanned or unwelcome compulsion in the past, पड़ता है a regular one, पड़ेगा a strong one in the future.
items.say: राज को चलकर दफ़्तर जाना पड़ा ।
items.en: Raj[0+1] {had to}[5] walk[2+4] {to the office}[3].

items.q: Fill the gap: “The girl who is singing is my sister (lit. “… she …”).”
items.hi: ___ लड़की गा रही है, वह मेरी बहिन है ।
items.say: जो लड़की गा रही है, वह मेरी बहिन है ।
items.en: The girl[1] who[0] {is singing}[2+3+4] is[8] my[6] sister[7] (lit. “… she[5] …”).
wrong: कौन
कौन is the question word “who?”. The relative “who” is जो.
जिस
जिस is the oblique form, used before a postposition. Nothing follows लड़की here, so जो.
items.why: जो “(the one) who, which” opens the relative clause, and वह (plural वे) picks it up in the correlative clause.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The boy who came to our house yesterday is Sangeeta's brother (lit. “… he …”).”
items.hi: जो लड़का कल हमारे घर आया था, ___ संगीता का भाई है ।
items.say: जो लड़का कल हमारे घर आया था, वह संगीता का भाई है ।
items.en: The boy[1] who[0] came[5+6] to our[3] house[4] yesterday[2] is[11] Sangeeta's[8+9] brother[10] (lit. “… he[7] …”).
wrong: जो
जो opens the relative clause. The correlative clause takes वह.
उसने
ने is used only with a transitive verb in the perfective. The correlative is the subject of है — वह.
items.why: जो “(the one) who, which” opens the relative clause, and वह (plural वे) picks it up in the correlative clause.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The man who built this house now lives in Delhi (lit. “… he …”).”
items.hi: ___ आदमी ने यह घर बनाया, वह अब दिल्ली में रहता है ।
items.say: जिस आदमी ने यह घर बनाया, वह अब दिल्ली में रहता है ।
items.en: The man[1] who[0+2] built[5] this[3] house[4] now[7] lives[10+11] in Delhi[8+9] (lit. “… he[6] …”).
wrong: जो
Before ने the relative is oblique: जिस आदमी ने.
किस
किस is the oblique of the question word कौन. The relative is जिस.
items.why: Before a postposition जो becomes जिस (singular) or जिन (plural): जिसने, जिसे, जिन्होंने, जिन्हें. These match उसने, उसे, उन्होंने, उन्हें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Thank the one who cooked the food.”
items.hi: ___ खाना बनाया, उसे धन्यवाद दो ।
items.say: जिसने खाना बनाया, उसे धन्यवाद दो ।
items.en: Thank[4+5] the one[3] who[0] cooked[2] the food[1].
wrong: जो
Before ने the relative is oblique: जिसने.
किसने
किसने is the question “who (did)?”. The relative is जिसने.
जोने
Not a word. Before ने the relative is oblique, जिसने.
items.why: Before a postposition जो becomes जिस (singular) or जिन (plural): जिसने, जिसे, जिन्होंने, जिन्हें. These match उसने, उसे, उन्होंने, उन्हें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “People who come late won't get food (lit. “… they …”).”
items.hi: जो लोग देर से आएँगे, ___ खाना नहीं मिलेगा ।
items.say: जो लोग देर से आएँगे, उन्हें खाना नहीं मिलेगा ।
items.en: People[1] who[0] come[4] late[2+3] {won't get}[7+8] food[6] (lit. “… they[5] …”).
wrong: वे
The correlative takes the case its own clause needs: with मिलना the receiver takes को, so उन्हें.
जिन्हें
जिन्हें is a relative. The correlative begins with u-, उन्हें.
items.why: The relative and the correlative each take the case their own clause needs. मिलना “to be got, be available”: the thing received is the subject and the verb agrees with it. The receiver takes को, never ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children who can sing will sing at school tomorrow (lit. “… they …”).”
items.hi: ___ बच्चों को गाना आता है, वे कल स्कूल में गाएँगे ।
items.say: जिन बच्चों को गाना आता है, वे कल स्कूल में गाएँगे ।
items.en: The children[1] who[0] {can sing}[2+3+4+5] {will sing}[10] at school[8+9] tomorrow[7] (lit. “… they[6] …”).
wrong: जिस
जिस is singular. बच्चों is plural: जिन.
जो
Before को the relative is oblique: जिन बच्चों को.
जिसों
Not a word. The plural oblique of जो is जिन.
items.why: Before a postposition जो becomes जिस (singular) or जिन (plural): जिसने, जिसे, जिन्होंने, जिन्हें. These match उसने, उसे, उन्होंने, उन्हें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The people who helped us are my old friends (lit. “… they …”).”
items.hi: ___ हमारी मदद की, वे मेरे पुराने दोस्त हैं ।
items.say: जिन्होंने हमारी मदद की, वे मेरे पुराने दोस्त हैं ।
items.en: The people who[0] helped[2+3] us[1] are[8] my[5] old[6] friends[7] (lit. “… they[4] …”).
wrong: जिसने
जिसने is singular. वे … हैं shows the people are plural: जिन्होंने.
जिन
Before ने the plural relative is जिन्होंने (or जिन + noun + ने).
जोओं
Not a word. जो does not take the noun ending -õ. Its plural oblique is जिन, and before ने जिन्होंने.
items.why: Before a postposition जो becomes जिस (singular) or जिन (plural): जिसने, जिसे, जिन्होंने, जिन्हें. These match उसने, उसे, उन्होंने, उन्हें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will wear the sari that Mother gave me at the wedding (lit. “… it …”). (a woman speaking)”
items.hi: जो साड़ी माँ ने मुझे दी थी, ___ मैं शादी में पहनूँगी ।
items.say: जो साड़ी माँ ने मुझे दी थी, उसे मैं शादी में पहनूँगी ।
items.en: I[8] {will wear}[11] the sari[1] that[0] Mother[2+3] gave[5+6] me[4] at[10] the wedding[9] (lit. “… it[7] …”). (a woman speaking)
wrong: जिसे
जिसे is a relative. The correlative begins with u-, उसे.
उसने
ने is used only in the perfective. पहनूँगी is future, so there is no ने.
items.why: The relative and the correlative each take the case their own clause needs.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Whoever passes this exam will get a book (lit. “… he …”).”
items.hi: जो ___ यह परीक्षा पास करेगा, उसे एक किताब मिलेगी ।
items.say: जो कोई यह परीक्षा पास करेगा, उसे एक किताब मिलेगी ।
items.en: Whoever[0+1] passes[4+5] this[2] exam[3] {will get}[9] a[7] book[8] (lit. “… he[6] …”).
wrong: कुछ
जो कुछ is “whatever”, for things. For people it is जो कोई.
किसी
किसी is the oblique of कोई. Nothing follows here, and the subject of करेगा is direct: जो कोई.
items.why: जो कोई “whoever, anyone who”, जो कुछ “whatever”, जो भी “whoever, whatever (emphatic)”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जो कुछ तुमने सीखा है, वह कभी मत भूलना ।
items.a: Never forget whatever you have learned.
wrong: Never forget whoever taught you.
जो कुछ is “whatever”, for things. “Whoever” is जो कोई.
You have never forgotten anything you learned.
मत भूलना is a command, “don't forget”, with the infinitive.
items.why: जो कुछ “whatever”, picked up by वह.

items.q: Join the two sentences with जो … वह
items.a: जो किताब मैंने ख़रीदी, वह बहुत महँगी थी ।
wrong: जिस किताब मैंने ख़रीदी, वह बहुत महँगी थी ।
No postposition follows किताब (ने goes with मैं), so the relative stays direct: जो.
जो किताब मैंने ख़रीदी, जो बहुत महँगी थी ।
The second clause takes the correlative वह.
items.why: जो “(the one) who, which” opens the relative clause, and वह (plural वे) picks it up in the correlative clause.
items.hi: मैंने एक किताब ख़रीदी । वह बहुत महँगी थी ।
items.say: जो किताब मैंने ख़रीदी, वह बहुत महँगी थी ।
items.en: The book[1] (that[0]) I[2] bought[3] was[7] very[5] expensive[6] (lit. “… it[4] …”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children got a holiday today.”
items.hi: बच्चों को आज छुट्टी ___ ।
items.say: बच्चों को आज छुट्टी मिली ।
items.en: The children[0+1] got[4] a holiday[3] today[2].
wrong: मिला
मिला is masculine. मिलना agrees with छुट्टी, the thing received.
मिलीं
मिलीं is plural. It is one holiday.
मिलया
Not a word. मिलना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is मिला, मिली, with no -y-.
items.why: मिलना “to be got, be available”: the thing received is the subject and the verb agrees with it. The receiver takes को, never ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You can get good milk in this village.”
items.hi: इस गाँव में अच्छा दूध ___ है ।
items.say: इस गाँव में अच्छा दूध मिलता है ।
items.en: {You can get}[5+6] good[3] milk[4] in[2] this[0] village[1].
wrong: मिलते
मिलते is plural. दूध is singular.
मिलती
मिलती is feminine. दूध is masculine.
items.why: मिलना can mean “to be available” without naming the receiver. मिलना “to be got, be available”: the thing received is the subject and the verb agrees with it. The receiver takes को, never ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj found an old book in the market.”
items.hi: बाज़ार में ___ एक पुरानी किताब मिली ।
items.say: बाज़ार में राज को एक पुरानी किताब मिली ।
items.en: Raj[2+3] found[7] an[4] old[5] book[6] in[1] the market[0].
wrong: राज ने
मिलना is intransitive: the receiver takes को, never ने.
राज
The receiver takes को — राज को. The book is the subject.
items.why: मिलना “to be got, be available”: the thing received is the subject and the verb agrees with it. The receiver takes को, never ने.

items.q: Which says you ran into Usha at the market by chance?
wrong: बाज़ार में मैं उषा से मिला ।
This is correct Hindi, but X से मिलना is a planned meeting. A chance encounter is मुझे उषा मिली.
बाज़ार में मुझे उषा मिला ।
मिलना agrees with उषा, the person met, who is a woman: मिली.
items.why: X को Y मिलना is an unplanned meeting, X Y से मिलना a planned one.
items.say: बाज़ार में मुझे उषा मिली ।
items.en: I[2] {ran into}[4] Usha[3] at[1] the market[0].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: राज अपने पिता से बहुत मिलता-जुलता है ।
items.a: Raj looks very much like his father.
wrong: Raj often meets his father.
मिलता-जुलता “resembling” is from मिलना-जुलना “to resemble”, not मिलना “to meet”.
Raj gets on well with his father.
मिलना-जुलना means “to resemble”.
items.why: मिलना-जुलना “to resemble”, with से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children cleaned the room together.”
items.hi: बच्चों ने ___ कमरा साफ़ किया ।
items.say: बच्चों ने मिल-जुलकर कमरा साफ़ किया ।
items.en: The children[0+1] cleaned[4+5] the room[3] together[2].
wrong: मिलना-जुलना
मिलना-जुलना is the verb “to resemble”. “Together” is मिल-जुलकर.
जान-बूझकर
जान-बूझकर is “deliberately”. “Together” is मिल-जुलकर.
items.why: मिल-जुलकर (or मिलकर), “having met and joined”, means “together”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How did you like my new sari?”
items.hi: तुम्हें मेरी नई साड़ी कैसी ___ ?
items.say: तुम्हें मेरी नई साड़ी कैसी लगी ?
items.en: {How did you like}[0+4+5] my[1] new[2] sari[3]?
wrong: लगा
लगा is masculine. लगना agrees with साड़ी, the thing that strikes you.
लगीं
लगीं is plural. It is one sari.
items.why: With लगना the person affected takes को, and the verb agrees with the thing felt or the thing that strikes them (भूख लगी, डर लगता है, फ़िल्म अच्छी लगी).

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children are very hungry now.”
items.hi: बच्चों को अब बहुत भूख ___ है ।
items.say: बच्चों को अब बहुत भूख लगी है ।
items.en: The children[0+1] are[6] very[3] hungry[4+5] now[2].
wrong: लगा
लगा is masculine. भूख is feminine.
लगे
लगे is plural. The subject is भूख, not बच्चों.
items.why: With लगना the person affected takes को, and the verb agrees with the thing felt or the thing that strikes them (भूख लगी, डर लगता है, फ़िल्म अच्छी लगी).

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am afraid of dogs.”
items.hi: मुझे कुत्तों से डर ___ है ।
items.say: मुझे कुत्तों से डर लगता है ।
items.en: I[0] {am afraid}[3+4+5] of[2] dogs[1].
wrong: लगती
लगती is feminine. डर is masculine.
लगते
लगते is plural. The subject is डर, not कुत्तों.
items.why: With लगना the person affected takes को, and the verb agrees with the thing felt or the thing that strikes them (भूख लगी, डर लगता है, फ़िल्म अच्छी लगी).

items.q: Fill the gap: “It takes eight hours to get from Lucknow to Banaras.”
items.hi: लखनऊ से बनारस पहुँचने में आठ घंटे ___ ।
items.say: लखनऊ से बनारस पहुँचने में आठ घंटे लगते हैं ।
items.en: It takes[7+8] eight[5] hours[6] to get[3+4] from Lucknow[0+1] to Banaras[2].
wrong: लगता है
लगता है is singular. आठ घंटे, the time taken, is the plural subject.
लगती हैं
लगती हैं is feminine. घंटे is masculine.
लगनेगा
Not a word. The future of लगना is built on the stem, लगेगा. Here the present लगते हैं is needed anyway.
items.why: Time taken: the oblique infinitive (-ne) + में, with the amount of time as the subject of लगना (दो घंटे लगते हैं).

items.q: Fill the gap: “It took me the whole day to write all these letters.”
items.hi: ये सब चिट्ठियाँ ___ में मुझे पूरा दिन लगा ।
items.say: ये सब चिट्ठियाँ लिखने में मुझे पूरा दिन लगा ।
items.en: It took[8] me[5] the whole[6] day[7] to write[3+4] all[1] these[0] letters[2].
wrong: लिखना
Before में the infinitive is oblique: लिखने.
लिखनी
लिखनी is the agreeing form used with चाहिए and पड़ना. Before में the infinitive is the oblique लिखने.
items.why: Time taken: the oblique infinitive (-ne) + में, with the amount of time as the subject of लगना (दो घंटे लगते हैं).

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: यह सवाल मुझे आसान नहीं लगता ।
items.a: This question doesn't seem easy to me.
wrong: I didn't ask this easy question.
लगना here is “to seem”. Nothing is asked.
This question isn't easy for me to ask.
लगना means “to seem”: the question seems hard.
items.why: लगना also means “to seem”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan got hurt yesterday.”
items.hi: कल मोहन को चोट ___ ।
items.say: कल मोहन को चोट लगी ।
items.en: Mohan[1+2] {got hurt}[3+4] yesterday[0].
wrong: लगा
लगा is masculine. चोट is feminine.
लगीं
लगीं is plural. It is one injury.
लगया
Not a word. लगना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is लगा, लगी, with no -y-.
items.why: With लगना the person affected takes को, and the verb agrees with the thing felt or the thing that strikes them (भूख लगी, डर लगता है, फ़िल्म अच्छी लगी).

items.en: We[0] should[5] sell[4] this[1] old[2] car[3].
wrong: बेचने
बेचने is masculine plural or oblique. The infinitive agrees with गाड़ी, feminine singular: बेचनी.
हमने
With चाहिए the person takes को — हमें.
बेचता
बेचता is the imperfective participle. चाहिए follows the infinitive.
चाहिता
Not a word. चाहिए never changes. चाहता, from चाहना, means “wants”.

items.en: I[0] {had to}[4] stay[3] {for two hours}[1+2].
wrong: पड़े
पड़े is plural, as if agreeing with घंटे. रुकना has no object, so पड़ना is masculine singular: पड़ा.
मैंने
With पड़ना the person takes को, so मुझे.

items.en: The woman[1] who[0] lives[3+4] upstairs[2] is[7] a doctor[6] (lit. “… she[5] …”).
wrong: कौन
कौन is the question word. The relative is जो.
रहता
रहता is masculine. औरत is a woman.

items.en: The girl[1] who[0+2] painted[5] this[3] picture[4] is[9] my[7] daughter[8] (lit. “… she[6] …”).
wrong: जो
Before ने the relative is oblique: जिस लड़की ने.
बनाया
बनाया is masculine. With ने the verb agrees with तस्वीर, feminine.
जोने
Not a word. Before ने the relative is oblique, जिस लड़की ने.

items.en: Pinki[8] {won't sleep}[9+10] until[0+1+4] the story[2] {is finished}[3+5] (lit. “… {until then}[6+7] …”).
wrong: से
जब से … तब से is “since”. “Until” is जब तक … नहीं … तब तक.
सोई
सोई is the perfective. The time is future, so सोएगी.

items.en: {Did you like}[0+1+3+4] the film[2]?
wrong: अच्छा
अच्छा is masculine. It agrees with फ़िल्म, feminine.
तुमने
लगना never takes ने. The person who likes takes को — तुम्हें.

items.en: Grandma[2+3] feels[5+6] the cold[4] {at night}[0+1].
wrong: लगता
लगता is masculine. The verb agrees with ठंड, feminine.
ने
लगना never takes ने. The person who feels takes को.

items.en: Learning[1+2] Bengali[0] takes[5+6] {a long}[3] time[4].
wrong: सीखना
Before में the infinitive is oblique: सीखने.
लगती
लगती is feminine. The verb agrees with समय, masculine.

items.en: We[0] {had to}[4] sell[3] our[1] house[2].
wrong: बेचनी
बेचनी is feminine. The infinitive agrees with घर, masculine: बेचना.
हमने
With पड़ना the person takes को — हमें.

items.en: {As soon as}[0+1] the bell[2] rang[3], the children[6] ran[7+9] out[8] (lit. “… {just then}[4+5] …”).
wrong: कैसे
कैसे is the question word “how?”. The relative is जैसे.
बजा
बजा is masculine. घंटी is feminine: बजी.

items.en: I[0] {ran into}[4] Sangeeta[3] at[2] the station[1].
wrong: मिला
मिला is masculine. मिलना agrees with संगीता, the person met.
मैंने
मिलना never takes ने. The person who meets by chance takes को — मुझे.

items.en: Where[3] {can you get}[4+5] good[1] tea[2] here[0]?
wrong: मिलता
मिलता is masculine. मिलना agrees with चाय, feminine.
अच्छा
अच्छा is masculine. चाय is feminine.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जब भी मैं उसे फ़ोन करता हूँ, वह घर पर नहीं होता ।
items.a: Whenever I phone him, he isn't at home.
wrong: When I phoned him, he wasn't at home.
करता हूँ and होता are habitual, and जब भी is “whenever”.
Since I phoned him, he hasn't been at home.
“Since” would be जब से … तब से.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हमें इलाहाबाद में दो दिन रुकना पड़ेगा ।
items.a: We'll have to stay in Allahabad for two days.
wrong: We should stay in Allahabad for two days.
“Should” would be चाहिए. पड़ेगा is “will have to”.
We stayed in Allahabad for two days.
पड़ेगा is future: “will have to”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उस बेचारे कुत्ते को चोट लगी है ।
wrong: That poor dog has hurt someone.
The dog takes को — it is the one the injury struck.
That poor dog is hungry.
“Hungry” would be भूख लगी है. चोट is “injury”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जिस दिन हम दिल्ली पहुँचे, उसी दिन बहुत बारिश हुई ।
items.a: The very day we reached Delhi, it rained a lot.
wrong: Every day we were in Delhi, it rained a lot.
जिस दिन … उसी दिन is “on the (very) day that”, one day.
The day before we reached Delhi, it rained a lot.
उसी दिन is “that very day”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: कल रात हमारे गाँव में एक दुकान में आग लग गई ।
items.a: Last night a shop in our village caught fire.
wrong: Last night a shop in our village was robbed.
“Robbed” would be चोरी हुई. आग लगना is “to catch fire”.
Last night a shop in our village closed.
आग is “fire”. आग लग गई is “caught fire”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: राज को मिठाई अच्छी लगती है, पर उसे नहीं खानी चाहिए ।
items.a: Raj likes sweets, but he shouldn't eat them.
wrong: Raj likes sweets, but he can't get them.
“Can't get” would be नहीं मिलती. खानी चाहिए is “should eat”.
Raj likes sweets, but he doesn't eat them.
नहीं खानी चाहिए is “shouldn't eat”, not a plain “doesn't eat”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मुझे गाँव में रहना अच्छा लगता है ।
items.a: I like living in the village.
wrong: I have to live in the village.
“Have to” would be रहना पड़ता है. अच्छा लगना is “to like”.
I should live in the village.
“Should” would be रहना चाहिए.

items.q: Relative words such as “who”, “when” and “as” begin with …
wrong: k- (कौन, कब, कैसे)
Those are question words.
t- or v- (तब, वह, वैसे)
Those are the correlatives that pick up the relative clause.
items.why: Relative words begin with j- (जो, जब), question words with k- (कौन, कब). English “wh-” words do both jobs.

items.q: In उसे हिन्दी सीखनी चाहिए, what does सीखनी agree with?
wrong: उसे, the person
The person takes को, and the verb never agrees with a word followed by को.
चाहिए, the word after it
चाहिए never changes. The infinitive agrees with a direct object without को, and हिन्दी is feminine, so सीखनी.
items.why: Infinitive + चाहिए “should, ought”: the person under the obligation takes को, and the infinitive agrees with a direct object (हिन्दी सीखनी, कपड़े धोने). In the past था, थी, थे or थीं is added, agreeing in the same way.

items.q: What does पड़ा suggest in मुझे जाना पड़ा ?
wrong: A moral duty
That is चाहिए — मुझे जाना चाहिए था.
A regular compulsion
That is the imperfective, जाना पड़ता था.
items.why: पड़ा is an unplanned or unwelcome compulsion in the past, पड़ता है a regular one, पड़ेगा a strong one in the future.

items.q: In जिस आदमी ने यह घर बनाया, वह अब दिल्ली में रहता है, why is the correlative वह and not उसने?
items.a: Each pronoun takes the case its own clause needs
wrong: The correlative always copies the relative's case
No. Here the relative is oblique before ने, while वह is the subject of an intransitive verb.
वह never takes ने
वह can take ने (उसने) when its own clause has a transitive perfective verb.
items.why: The relative and the correlative each take the case their own clause needs.

items.q: With मिलना “to get”, what is the grammatical subject?
wrong: The receiver
The receiver takes को — मुझे चिट्ठी मिली.
Nothing: मिलना has no subject
It has one, the thing received, and the verb agrees with it.
items.why: मिलना “to be got, be available”: the thing received is the subject and the verb agrees with it. The receiver takes को, never ने.

items.q: In चिट्ठी लिखने में दो घंटे लगे, what is the subject of लगे?
wrong: चिट्ठी
चिट्ठी is the object of लिखने. लगे is masculine plural, agreeing with दो घंटे.
लिखने
लिखने is the oblique infinitive before में. The time taken is the subject.
items.why: Time taken: the oblique infinitive (-ne) + में, with the amount of time as the subject of लगना (दो घंटे लगते हैं).

items.q: What does जब तक … नहीं … तब तक mean?
wrong: as long as … for that long
That is जब तक … तब तक without the negative.
since … since then
That is जब से … तब से.
items.why: The pairs are जब … तब “when … then”, जब से … तब से “since … since then”, जब तक … तब तक “as long as … for that long”, जब तक … नहीं … तब तक “until”, जैसे ही … वैसे ही “as soon as”.
